newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank no comment on Direct Line report.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank no comment on Direct Line report.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland Plc on Monday declined comment on a press report that its insurance unit Direct Line, which pioneered telephone-based insurance operations, fell into losses in its first half.
"The story is pure speculation, not based on any fact or contact with us," said a spokesman for the Edinburgh-based banking group.
A report in the Sunday Times said Royal Bank would report a loss for Direct Line in its interim results on May 7, reflecting a "vicious" price war and an increase in personal injury payouts.
The paper said this contrasted with analyst expectations of a small profit from the unit.
However, analysts said Direct Line's profits had been under pressure for the past year and the unit was not expected to make a significant contribution to Royal Bank's profits this year.
They also pointed out that the winter period covered by the company's forthcoming results was usually the toughest time for the auto insurance sector, a big proportion of Direct Line's business.
"I don't think it would be a huge shock to find Direct Line in the red at the half year," said analyst Ian McEwan at Lehman Brothers.
"I don't know of anyone who has been forecasting a loss for the full year but if it reported a loss I don't think it would make a huge difference to Royal Bank profits," McEwan said.
"The question remains how much red ink needs to be written before Direct Line moves back into profits...it is a good company in a rotten business."
